_comment: Which datasets support which task, and why. A dataset appears in a task only if it can actually support that task's claim. Generated 2026-09-09.

notes.reddit: Primary. Real labels and features, high homophily, largest measured CAAN recovery (+18.7pp). Report the majority-per-community control alongside it: Louvain communities are ~79% label-pure, so a zero-parameter predictor scores 0.7386.
notes.ogbn-arxiv: Medium scale; the dataset with verified genuine multi-community partitioning in existing artifacts (220 communities).
notes.ogbn-mag: Limitation case. Heterogeneous graph, Louvain severs meta-paths, recovery is poor. Keep and explain rather than drop.
notes.DeezerEurope: Optional heterophily contrast, which turns the homophily claim into a comparison rather than an assertion.

notes.shared_with_node_classification: reddit, ogbn-products and ogbn-mag appear in both tables so the two tasks are directly comparable.
notes.LiveJournal: Valid here — edges are real. Features are synthetic, so this is a purely structural task and must be labelled as such.
notes.open_issue: Two measurement paths disagree: standalone benchmark scripts report 0.812 (LiveJournal) / 0.785 (Orkut) on a ~400K-edge head slice with random features, while the EMR pipeline reports 0.517 / 0.525 on the full graph under a 30K-edge-per-community cap. Resolve before publishing either number.

notes.rationale: Scalability needs neither labels nor features, only wall-clock against executor count. This is where LiveJournal and Orkut are fully qualified.
notes.ogbn-papers100M: Extreme point. Requires LPA (Louvain is driver-bound) and the Phase 3 block-splitting path.

LiveJournal.reason: No node labels. experiment_config assigns 100 synthetic classes over synthetic features; EMR runs score ~1.07%, which is chance. The task does not exist for this graph.

Orkut.reason: No node labels. EMR runs score ~1.08%, chance for 100 classes.

appendix_only.reason: ML-GRL evaluated on these, so they enable direct comparison with prior work from the same group. Too small (11K-34K nodes) to carry a distributed-systems result, so keep them in an appendix comparability table rather than the main results.
